asks: What does a computer get when a secret is exchanged for a token?
answer: Silo knows the token endpoints of the providers that matter. When a computer exchanges a secret at one of them, the boundary makes the exchange with the real secret and gives the computer a placeholder for each token it gets back. It swaps the real token in on the way to the hosts that token is for, and refreshes it itself. A token from an endpoint Silo does not know reaches the computer as it is, and the app says so for that secret.
